vm.intro: Supply, political responsibility and the effects of your mandates, as recorded at this settlement.
vm.nochNicht: The results of your supply policy appear here after the first monthly settlement.
vm.vergleichHilfe: For each active decision, the same month is calculated once without that measure. Stocks, war, trade and all other decisions stay the same. Allocation guarantees appear under the government policy. Contributions cannot be added together and do not explain the entire change from the previous month.
vm.zeit.vorbereitung: Ready no earlier than {datum}. No delivery or repair effect in this settlement yet.
vm.zeit.beratung: Vote scheduled for {datum}. This proposal supplies no goods or repairs before approval.
vm.zeit.beendet: Expired on {datum}. Earlier stocks and lasting repairs remain part of the starting conditions; no new mandate is created this month.
vm.mechanik.ausgewogen: Civilian needs and fronts share reachable supplies. Government policy gives neither side exclusive priority.
vm.mechanik.zivil: Civilian needs are served first. The comparison shows what this priority changes at home and at the front relative to the previous policy.
vm.mechanik.militaer: Fronts receive supplies first. More reachable fuel for operations can come at the expense of civilian supply.
vm.mechanik.schutz: Mandatory savings reduce gas and oil demand; export restrictions keep essential goods at home. Steel, electronics and fertiliser output also falls. Higher coverage can result from lower demand.
vm.mechanik.energie: Additional gas only fills procurement gaps. It can reach consumers now or build stocks; blocked transport routes still apply.
vm.mechanik.netz: Safe damaged corridors are repaired. The comparison shows the effect of this month’s repairs; occupied routes stay closed.
vm.gas: Additional imports from {land}: {menge} bn m³. Included price premium: {preis} bn USD.
vm.referenzKurs: Compared with the previous policy “{kurs}” under the same monthly conditions. Older saves use balanced allocation as the reference.
vm.referenzProgramm: Compared with this month without the active programme. Other measures remain in place.
vm.engpassHilfe: The three lowest coverage levels this month. Supply disruptions are recorded pressures, but do not by themselves explain every shortage.
vm.lieferausfall: War or sanctions disrupt supplies from: {laender}.
vm.hormus: Disruption in Hormuz affects these imports.
vm.andereEngpaesse: Available supplies, inputs or regional transport capacity cannot cover all demand.
vm.altbericht: This older report has no saved decision comparisons. They will be recorded from the next monthly settlement.
vm.anlass.unterversorgung: Civilian coverage is {deckung}%, below 90%. This triggers criticism even if supply has improved since the previous month.
vm.anlass.erholung: Coverage is at least 90% and has improved by {delta}. Recovery of more than two percentage points increases backing among supporting factions.
vm.anlass.kaumAenderung: Coverage is at least 90%, but has not improved by more than two percentage points. This monthly report therefore triggers no additional faction response.
vm.anlass.erstbericht: At least 90% of needs are met. Without a previous monthly value, recovery cannot yet be demonstrated, so no additional faction bonus is awarded.
vm.anlass.keinMandat: No parliament-backed programme is active in this settlement yet. It therefore creates no additional response from supporters or the opposition.
vm.kontrolle: Agreed parliamentary oversight doubles the monthly response: normally {n} readiness points per supporting faction, and personal loyalty for coalition partners.
vm.ohneKontrolle: Without enhanced oversight, the standard monthly response applies: normally {n} readiness points per supporting faction, and personal loyalty for coalition partners.
vm.traegerHilfe: Responsibility lies with factions whose own MPs mostly voted for the active mandate. Not every coalition faction supported it. The changes shown are those actually applied. Your own party receives no additional readiness bonus.
vm.anfrage: The opposition ({parteien}) demands accountability for shortages through a parliamentary question. Actual increase in opposition strength: {n} points.
vm.keinZugewinn: This supply report gives the opposition ({parteien}) no additional strength and triggers no new supply-related question. Other political conflicts continue independently.
vm.keineOpposition: This parliament currently has no faction outside the governing bloc, so no additional opposition question is raised.
vm.oppositionTraegt: An opposition faction may have supported the mandate and still demand accountability. Its readiness to support the mandate and collective opposition strength are separate political consequences.
vm.folgenrechnung: Break down trust and other effects
vm.vertrauen.ergebnis: Supply change from the previous month
vm.vertrauen.front: Military priority during civilian oil shortages
vm.grenzen: All values refer to this supply settlement. Values at the limits of 0 and 100 can only respond partially. Other systems also affect poverty, legitimacy and trust.
vm.anlass.knappUnterversorgung: Civilian coverage is just below 90%. The threshold has not yet been reached, so criticism continues even though rounding would put the display close to 90%.
vm.bruch.partei: {partei} left: {name} had {loyalitaet} loyalty, below the departure threshold of {grenze}. The governing coalition lost {sitze} seats.
vm.bruch.mehrheit: The coalition retained a numerical seat majority. This does not guarantee support for individual bills.
vm.bruch.luecke: After the review, the coalition was {n} seats short of the 301-seat majority. Temporary backing and support for individual bills require separate negotiations.
vm.bruch.abfolge: The supply assessment above preceded this review; its party roles reflect that earlier point. Departure depends on loyalty after the monthly effects booked up to that point. The supply compromise is therefore not necessarily the sole cause.
vm.bruch.handeln: A conversation does not restore a terminated alliance. In Parliament, under Factions, review a new coalition or temporary backing with its costs and promises. This report preserves the position at the time.
